newsitem.title: GERMANY: Veba buys 36.4 pct stake in Degussa.
newsitem.headline: Veba buys 36.4 pct stake in Degussa.

text.p: Diversified German utilities group Veba AG said on Wednesday it would buy a 36.4 percent stake in Degussa AG, making it the largest shareholder.
Veba said it was buying Chemiewerte mbH, which held the Degussa stake, for 2.9 billion marks, or 86.80 marks a share. Previous owners of Chemiewerte were Henkel KGaA, Dresdner Bank AG and Munich Re.
Degussa and the sellers later confirmed the transaction.
Veba and Degussa, the chemicals and metals group, said they shared the view that Degussa should maintain its successful business strategy and continue to be traded on German exchanges.
The transaction is subject to the approval of cartel authorities.
Veba said the acquisition opens possibilities for cooperation between Degussa and Huels, Veba's own chemicals division.
Both chemicals groups are trying to boost productivity and concentrate on core businesses to become more internationally competitive.

The Veba statement quoted chairman Ulrich Hartmann, as saying Degussa could continue its activities in hydrogen peroxide, cyanide, and automotive catalyzers, among others, where it is among the world leaders.
"I see the transaction as an opportunity to strengthen our chemicals activities," Hartmann said.
Henkel held 16.6 percent of Degussa, while Dresdner and Munich Re held 9.9 percent each.
